name: card-01
title: I. Codebase
tagline: One codebase tracked in revision control, many deploys
rule: One app is one repository. Many deploys (dev, staging, production) run the same codebase at different commits. Shared code becomes a library, never a second copy.
practice: One Spring Boot service per repository on the git host; main is protected; features on short-lived branches merged through pull requests; releases are tags.
check: A git checkout with exactly one remote on the git host, a main branch, no nested repositories.
fix: Create the repository, push main, protect it, move shared code to a dependency.

name: card-02
title: II. Dependencies
rule: Every dependency is declared in a manifest and isolated from the host; nothing implicit from the system is assumed.
practice: pom.xml declares everything, the Maven wrapper is committed, no SNAPSHOT versions on main, dependency:analyze is clean.
check: Wrapper present, no SNAPSHOT dependencies, dependency:analyze reports no used-undeclared dependency.
fix: Commit the wrapper, add the used dependency to pom.xml, pin released versions.

name: card-03
title: III. Config
rule: Everything that varies between deploys (credentials, hostnames, per-deploy values) comes from environment variables. The codebase could be open-sourced without leaking a credential. No grouped 'environments' in files.
practice: application.yml binds each deploy value with ${ENV_VAR:default}; @ConfigurationProperties for typed groups; no application-prod.yml with secrets.
check: No literal credentials or hostnames in main resources; datasource url environment-bound.
fix: Replace the literal with ${ENV_VAR:default} and document the variable in the README.

name: card-04
title: IV. Backing services
tagline: Treat backing services as attached resources
rule: Databases, queues, caches, mail are attached resources addressed by a URL in the config; swapping a local for a managed instance changes no code.
practice: spring.datasource.url and friends from DATABASE_URL; compose.yaml runs the same engine locally; no embedded database in the runtime scope.
check: Backing-service settings environment-bound, compose file present, no H2/HSQL at runtime.
fix: Bind the setting to an environment variable and add the service to compose.yaml.

name: card-05
title: V. Build, release, run
tagline: Strictly separate build and run stages
rule: Build turns the code into an immutable artifact; release combines the artifact with config; run starts the release. Nothing is built or changed at run time.
practice: Multi-stage Dockerfile; the run stage holds only the JRE and the extracted jar; bin/build-image.sh tags the image by commit; a release is image plus environment.
check: Two stages, no build tool in the run stage, a build script that tags by commit.
fix: Split the Dockerfile, remove build tooling from the run stage, tag images by git SHA.

name: card-06
title: VI. Processes
tagline: Execute the app as one or more stateless processes
rule: Processes are stateless and share nothing; anything that must persist lives in a backing service. Sticky sessions are a violation.
practice: No HttpSession state (Spring Session with a store if needed), no local file writes, no static mutable collections.
check: No session usage, no local file writes, no static mutable collections in main code.
fix: Move the state to the database or a cache service; make the process reentrant.

name: card-07
title: VII. Port binding
rule: The app is self-contained and exports HTTP by binding a port; it does not rely on a container injected at run time.
practice: Embedded server, server.port from PORT, jar packaging, EXPOSE in the Dockerfile.
check: server.port environment-bound, jar packaging, EXPOSE declared.
fix: Bind server.port to ${PORT:8080}, package as jar, add EXPOSE.

name: card-08
title: VIII. Concurrency
tagline: Scale out via the process model
rule: Scale by running more processes of each type; never daemonize or rely on a single instance.
practice: Replicas are interchangeable: cluster-safe scheduling (ShedLock) or none, shared caches, the JVM sized by the container.
check: No unlocked @Scheduled, no in-memory cache manager, MaxRAMPercentage in the entrypoint.
fix: Add a cluster lock or move the job to a worker; use an external cache; size the JVM relative to the container.

name: card-09
title: IX. Disposability
tagline: Maximize robustness with fast startup and graceful shutdown
rule: Processes start in seconds and stop gracefully on SIGTERM: stop taking requests, finish in-flight work, exit. Jobs are reentrant.
practice: server.shutdown=graceful with a grace period, exec-form entrypoint so the signal reaches the JVM, lean startup.
check: Graceful shutdown configured with a timeout, exec-form ENTRYPOINT, measured startup seconds.
fix: Set server.shutdown and spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase, use the JSON-array entrypoint.

name: card-10
title: X. Dev/prod parity
tagline: Keep development, staging, and production as similar as possible
rule: Close the gaps: deploy soon after writing, the same people deploy who wrote, the same backing services everywhere. No lightweight substitutes locally.
practice: Postgres in compose.yaml and in Testcontainers, never H2 in tests; continuous small merges.
check: Compose runs the production engine, tests use Testcontainers, no embedded test database.
fix: Replace the substitute with the real engine through compose and Testcontainers.

name: card-11
title: XI. Logs
rule: The app never manages log files; it writes an unbuffered stream to stdout and the environment routes it.
practice: Structured (ECS/JSON) console logging, no file appenders, no System.out.
check: No file appender or logging.file.*, structured console format, no System.out logging.
fix: Remove file appenders, enable logging.structured.format.console, log through the logger.

name: card-12
title: XII. Admin processes
tagline: Run admin/management tasks as one-off processes
rule: Migrations and one-off tasks run as processes of the same release, in the same environment, from code shipped with the app.
practice: Flyway migrations versioned in db/migration; APP_TASK=<task> runs a one-off process of the same image and exits.
check: Migration tool present, versioned migration files, an admin-task runner keyed by the environment.
fix: Add Flyway with a versioned baseline and an ApplicationRunner that runs APP_TASK and exits.
